opening.argument: The video provides concrete instruction for using Microsoft Teams in an educational setting. It explains how to join a scheduled class meeting, including adjusting video and audio settings before joining, and shows how users can create teams for “group projects, clubs, activities, and more.” It further explains that channels can divide a project into multiple parts. The title identifies the subject as working with classes and classmates in Microsoft Teams, while the displayed interface shows class and group tiles alongside team and channel creation controls. These features establish ordinary software guidance and product education, with encouragement to use Teams and related support resources consistent with routine technology promotion.

citations.quote: To join a scheduled class meeting, select your calendar, join, then join now after you've adjusted your video and audio settings.
But you can also create your own teams too, which is great for group projects, clubs, activities, and more.
If your project has multiple parts, add channels to break them up.
Working with classes and classmates in Microsoft Teams
